extracted.intended_audience: hospital quality leaders, measure developers, EHR vendors, payers, health IT specialists, and public commenters on CMS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for proposing, testing, endorsing, implementing, and publicly reporting Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program measures (examples: Diabetes EDAC and Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQMs). Includes operational, technical, statistical, and policy considerations CMS seeks comment on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational feasibility (implementation burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how feasible it would be for hospitals, especially those in rural areas, to implement and report the measure using existing data and workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS asks respondents to describe data, workflow, or resource challenges and to identify the single most important change recommended to enable implementation. Consider staffing, IT, training, and resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: EHR-claims reconciliation and FHIR representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether EHRs receive reconciled claims codes from payers/billing systems and whether EHR data reflect claims-adjudicated codes or remain unchanged after claims submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any time lags or other considerations for using claims codes for surveillance and measure calculation; if reconciled claims are received, indicate whether they can be represented in FHIR APIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party vendor reconciliation and data flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the role of third-party vendors (quality measurement vendors, HIEs, aggregators, EHR intermediaries) in reconciling claims (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS) with clinical or FHIR-based data for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how vendors receive and submit data, what standards they use, and the frequency and cadence of data flows; include examples of vendor-mediated normalization/reconciliation workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping EHR data to measure-specific FHIR profiles and value sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify anticipated challenges in mapping EHR data to the specified Sepsis (or other) measure FHIR profiles and value sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on data elements that may be unstructured (narrative), represented in local codes, or exist outside commonly used documents (e.g., flowsheets, provider orders). CMS refers to NHSN digital quality measure resources (HL7 NHSN-DQM and CDC NHSN FHIR IG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of enabling FHIR access and linking claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate additional anticipated challenges or burdens related to: making required EHR data available in FHIR; accessing and linking claims data needed for exclusions and risk adjustment; and working with vendors or NHSN to implement dQM specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed descriptions of technical and operational barriers, costs, and timelines for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and comparability across hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess to what extent the proposed measure allows for fair comparison across hospitals and identify adjustments or stratifications to improve fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider case mix, sociodemographic factors, access differences, and other hospital/system-level factors that might require stratification or adjustment to ensure equitable comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for pay-for-performance (meaningful reflection of quality/value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the measure meaningfully reflects quality/value of care and whether CMS should consider including it in pay-for-performance programs (e.g., Hospital VBP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential unintended effects of using the measure for payment adjustment (e.g., risk variable selection issues, reduced access to care, documentation burden), and describe mitigation strategies if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory endorsement requirement and exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures specified by the Secretary for the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program generally must be endorsed by the entity contracted under section 1890(a) (CBE); however, an exception exists when no feasible, practical endorsed measure exists for a specified area/topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where exception applies, the Secretary may specify a non-endorsed measure provided due consideration is given to measures endorsed or adopted by a consensus organization identified by the Secretary. CMS will submit measures to the CBE for endorsement when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-rulemaking review and Recommendation Group voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures undergo a pre-rulemaking review via the Partnership for Quality Measurement, with Recommendation and Advisory Groups voting to recommend or not recommend measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reports vote counts and summarizes voters' considerations and rationales; lack of consensus does not preclude adoption but informs further testing/specification or submission for endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reliability expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed measures must demonstrate reliability that meets accepted standards for a publicly reported measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing should include signal-to-noise or other reliability metrics over the applicable performance period (e.g., two years), and results should indicate adequate reliability for public reporting; example: Postoperative VTE had signal-to-noise reliability scores ~0.9998–0.9999 over 2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure validity expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure testing should demonstrate validity, including associations with measures in the same causal pathway and face validity as judged by stakeholders (TEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence from testing (construct/convergent validity), TEP feedback on face validity, and data-element validity where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator definition — Diabetes EDAC (days in acute care)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator is the number of days a patient spends in acute care for any cause within 30 days of discharge from the index diabetes hospitalization (ED visits without admission, observation stays, and unplanned readmissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting rules: each ED visit counts as one full day regardless of duration, observation stays measured in hours rounded up to nearest whole day (e.g., 28 hours = 2 days), readmissions counted by length of stay; multiple eligible encounters within 30 days all counted; planned readmissions are excluded per a planned readmission algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator definition — Diabetes EDAC (cohort inclusion/exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator includes index admissions meeting: principal discharge diagnosis of diabetes; enrolled in Medicare FFS or MA for 12 months prior and during admission; aged 65 or over; discharged alive from non-federal short-term acute care hospital; not transferred to another acute care facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions: less than 30 days post-discharge enrollment, discharged against medical advice, diabetes admissions within 30 days of a prior diabetes index admission. These mirror existing EDAC measures' criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment requirements — Diabetes EDAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjust for patient-level factors to account for case mix differences, including age, comorbidities, severity of illness, and frailty based on clinical status at index admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude complications that arise during hospitalization from covariates; account for survival times shorter than 30 days post-discharge; report discrimination (e.g., c-statistic) and predictive ability ranges from testing. Example testing showed c-statistics ~0.68/0.70 and predictive ability ranges reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure calculation — EDAC formula and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate final Diabetes EDAC score as the difference between a hospital's 'predicted days' and 'expected days' per 100 discharges (excess days), multiplied by 100; lower (including negative) scores indicate better performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow existing EDAC methodology used for pneumonia, heart failure, and AMI; interpret percentiles such that lower percentiles are better performing hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources, submission, performance period, and public reporting — EDAC
rubrics_metrics.description: EDAC uses Medicare FFS claims and Medicare Advantage encounter data and Medicare Enrollment Database for enrollment/vital status; hospitals are not required to submit additional data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes shortening performance period to 2 years and including MA beneficiaries; measure would be publicly reported via the Compare tool (or successor) on an annual basis using a rolling 24-month performance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance period specification (general proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to move existing EDAC measures from a 3-year to a 2-year performance period and to include Medicare Advantage beneficiaries in cohorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for FY 2029 payment determination, performance period July 1, 2025–June 30, 2027; reporting annually with rolling 24-month data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator definition — Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator is inpatient hospitalizations for adults who had an OR surgical procedure during the admission and experienced a postoperative VTE during hospitalization or within 30 days after the first surgical procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifiable via documentation of VTE not present on admission; or imaging followed by an order for anticoagulation; or a subsequent hospital stay within 30 days with VTE documentation and anticoagulation order/prescription. See Partnership for Quality Measurement specifications for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator definition — Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator is adult inpatient hospitalizations with a surgical procedure performed in the operating room during the encounter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: obstetric-related diagnoses; VTE present on admission; acute brain or spinal injury/hemorrhage present on admission; ECMO during encounter; thrombectomy before or on same day as first surgical procedure; intracranial or spinal surgery with discharge <5 days after surgery; inpatient encounters with duration of stay <2 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment requirements — Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjust for factors affecting VTE risk: age, sex, and eight clinical factors (bleeding disorders, cancer, catheter insertion, history of VTE, obesity, respiratory operations, stroke, vascular surgeries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk model development used two years of EHR data; testing should demonstrate discrimination between high-risk and low-risk patients and ensure fair evaluation of hospitals caring for higher-risk populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure testing sample size, reliability, and data-element validity expectations — Postoperative VTE
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing should report sample characteristics (number of hospitalizations, hospitals, states) and demonstrate reliability and data-element validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sample of 100,911 hospitalizations from 34 hospitals; reliability (signal-to-noise) ranged 0.9998–0.9999 over 2 years; data-element validity testing with chart abstraction should show agreement between EHR data and chart-abstracted data for denominator/numerator classification; document sensitivities/specificities and explain any limitations (e.g., low sensitivity for denominator exclusions due to testing sample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder feedback and measure refinement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate feedback from Recommendation Group and Technical Expert Panel, including suggested modifications and concerns, into measure refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common considerations include shortening the accountability window (e.g., to 7 days), adding sociodemographic risk factors, expanding to hospital-wide measures versus condition-specific, further testing, clarifying specifications, and pursuing endorsement. CMS may respond to concerns by explaining testing results or planning further submission to CBE.
